name: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited

profile.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company (TSMC) is the world's largest dedicated semiconductor foundry. It makes leading-edge logic chips for NVIDIA, Apple, AMD, Broadcom, Qualcomm, and the hyperscalers' custom AI accelerators. Morris Chang founded it in 1987 and invented the pure-play foundry model. Q3 2026 revenue was $46.7B, up 41.2% YoY in USD, at a 66.4% gross margin, and management expects full-year 2026 USD growth above 40%. C.C. Wei is Chairman and CEO.

innovation.label: STRONG
innovation.analysis: Track Record (3/3): TSMC has ramped N5 (2020), N3 (2023), and N2 (2025-26) in sequence, and its CoWoS advanced packaging became the bottleneck technology of the AI buildout. Its revenue mix has shifted from smartphone-led to HPC/AI-led [1][3]. AI Deployment (2/2): TSMC manufactures nearly every frontier AI accelerator, and management projects AI accelerator revenue to grow at a 54-56% CAGR from 2024 to 2029, up from a prior 45% estimate [3]. Market Share (2/2): TSMC holds roughly two-thirds of global foundry revenue and well over 90% of sub-5nm production. Samsung and Intel Foundry have not closed the gap [2][3]. Pipeline (2/2): N2 is in steep volume ramp, which management says will dilute gross margin by 3-4 points. A16 follows, and 2026 capex was raised to $60-64B from $52-56B to meet AI demand [1][2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D is about 7% of revenue, which is above other foundries and the largest absolute process-technology R&D budget in the industry [5].

inspiration.label: STRONG
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (4/4): TSMC aims to be 'the trusted technology and capacity provider of the global logic IC industry'. Its 39-year pure-play foundry model has proven that purpose: by promising never to compete with customers, it made the entire fabless industry, NVIDIA included, possible [4]. Community Impact (1/2): The TSMC Education and Culture Foundation and the TSMC Charity Foundation fund STEM and community programs in Taiwan. We found no dollar-scaled program that sets TSMC apart from other large companies [7]. Employee Retention (1/2): Wei says TSMC hires about 9,000 people a year, screens them for 'integrity first, then innovation and commitment', and paid out large profit-sharing bonus increases in 2026 [4]. However, the fab culture is known for demanding hours, and we found no independent turnover data that would justify full credit. Insider Buying (1/2): We could not verify meaningful net open-market buying by executives in the last 12 months. Insider activity is mostly compensation-related, so this item scores neutral.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Scored mechanically as a Growth holding (sleeve forced by portfolios.json): 10.0 of 10 weighted points. Every metric meets or beats its target: D/E of 11.6%, ROE of 41.9% (double weight), TTM revenue growth of 50.9%, and a 5-year revenue CAGR of 23.3% from NT$1.34T in 2020 to NT$3.81T in 2025 (double weight) [5]. Forward P/E is 18.5, profit margin is 51.1%, and Forward PEG is 0.80 (double weight) [5]. Q3 2026 operating margin of 58.7% shows how much pricing power TSMC has in leading-edge capacity [1]. Liquidity is about $4.5B per day.

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (9/9): TSMC is the physical foundation of AI. Every frontier model needs leading-edge silicon and CoWoS packaging that only TSMC supplies at scale, and Wei says CoWoS demand is growing about 80% a year [3]. Analysts' worries about TSMC concern geopolitics, tariffs, and a possible AI capex overbuild, not AI substituting for its service [3][6]. AI Opportunity (1/1): AI and HPC are TSMC's largest and fastest-growing platform. Management guides to a 54-56% AI accelerator revenue CAGR through 2029 and raised full-year 2026 growth guidance to above 40% on AI demand [2][3].

infinite_game.summary: TSMC is one of the clearest infinite players in global industry. Its founding promise to be a trusted partner that never competes with its customers has held for 39 years, through a founder succession and several semiconductor cycles. Leadership keeps spending heavily through downturns and frames success as enabling the ecosystem. The main gap is organizational: the culture is demanding, and the evidence that employees feel psychologically safe is not strong enough for full credit.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (3/3): The pure-play foundry model, under which TSMC exists to make other people's innovations possible, is service-oriented, inclusive, and has lasted 39 years. Wei has said any successor must share the values of 'technology leadership, capacity expansion, and customer trust', which shows the cause outranks any single leader [3][4].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (2/2): TSMC raised 2026 capex to $60-64B even though the higher spend weighed on sentiment, and it accepted 3-4 points of N2 margin dilution to stay ahead on process technology [1][2]. It has a long pattern of counter-cyclical investment, including record capex through the 2009 and 2023 downturns.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Leadership has been very continuous: Wei has been at TSMC for more than 28 years and succeeded founder Morris Chang smoothly. In 2026 the company raised employee profit-sharing by about 30% [3][4]. Offsetting this, there are persistent reports of long hours and a rigid hierarchy, and U.S. fab staff have described cultural friction in Arizona. That points to adequate rather than exceptional trust.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): TSMC created an industry by spinning out the foundry model in 1987. It later moved from being a wafer supplier to offering advanced packaging (CoWoS, SoIC) and a geographically spread manufacturing base in Arizona, Japan, and Germany, accepting lower overseas margins to keep its customers' trust [1][2].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Management describes Samsung and Intel as serious competitors that drive its own execution, and it frames its position around earning customer trust rather than destroying rivals. TSMC has also stuck to its pledge not to compete with its customers [3].

investment_thesis: TSMC is the only company that can make frontier AI silicon at scale, and the numbers show it. Q3 2026 revenue was $46.7B (up 41.2% YoY), gross margin was 66.4%, and operating margin was 58.7%, all above guidance [1]. Management raised full-year 2026 USD growth to above 40% and expects a 54-56% AI accelerator revenue CAGR through 2029 [2][3]. Even so, the stock trades at 18.5x forward earnings with a 0.80 PEG, a 51% net margin, and 12% D/E [5].
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on concentration and capital intensity. 2026 capex of $60-64B, with Morgan Stanley estimating $75-80B for 2027, assumes AI demand lasts; a hyperscaler spending pause would leave TSMC with expensive idle capacity [2]. The N2 ramp and overseas fabs will dilute gross margin by several points, and nearly all leading-edge capacity still sits in Taiwan, about 100 miles from mainland China [1]. Water and power limits are also real: TSMC used about 8% of Taiwan's electricity in 2023, and environmental groups have challenged new Kaohsiung fabs [6].
key_catalysts: N2 volume ramp and A16 introduction lifting average wafer prices; Q4 2026 guidance is a 65-67% gross margin despite N2 dilution
CoWoS capacity roughly tripling to meet AI accelerator demand growing about 80% a year, which unlocks more AI revenue
Arizona fab ramp diversifying the manufacturing base and lowering U.S. tariff and geopolitical risk for U.S. customers
key_risks: Taiwan Strait geopolitical risk: most leading-edge capacity is in Taiwan, and any blockade or conflict would halt global AI chip supply
AI capex cycle risk: 2026 capex of $60-64B, possibly rising to $75-80B in 2027, assumes durable hyperscaler demand, and a pause would hurt utilization and margins
Margin dilution from overseas fabs and the N2 ramp (3-4 points), plus U.S. tariff and export-control policy uncertainty
